name: Dappled Diaphyseal Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Dappled Diaphyseal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic dappled or mottled sclerosis of the diaphyses on radiographs
Bowing deformities of long bones, especially the femur and tibia
Relative sparing of metaphyses with predominant diaphyseal involvement
Lack of systemic involvement such as neurological or hematological abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic radiologic dappled diaphyseal sclerosis plus bowing deformities of long bones
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological supported by clinical presentation; genetic testing may be supportive but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic mottled bone density pattern localized to diaphyses
searchTerms: speckled or patchy hardening of long bone shafts on X-ray
dappled sclerosis in diaphysis seen on radiographs
patchy bone hardening in long bone shafts
bowing deformities of arms or legs
one limb shorter than the other

common.symptomName: Bone pain localized to affected diaphyses
searchTerms: bone pain in shaft areas of long bones
localized pain in diaphyseal bone regions
pain in middle parts of long bones

common.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness adjacent to affected bones
searchTerms: mild stiffness in joints near affected bones
slight joint stiffness adjacent to bone lesions
broken long bones in affected areas

occasional.symptomName: Localized muscle weakness adjacent to affected bones
searchTerms: localized muscle weakness adjacent to bone lesions
weak muscles next to diseased bones

occasional.symptomName: Mild fatigue related to musculoskeletal discomfort
searchTerms: mild tiredness due to muscle and bone discomfort
fragile bones breaking easily with slow healing

laboratory: Normal serum calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase levels
Normal hematological parameters in most cases
imaging: Radiographs showing characteristic dappled or mottled sclerosis localized to diaphyses of long bones
Relative sparing of metaphyses and epiphyses
Bow-shaped deformities of femur and tibia
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; etiology currently unknown or idiopathic
other: Clinical examination revealing bowing deformities without systemic involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse diaphyseal sclerosis with cortical thickening
Linear striations of metaphyses and diaphyses rather than dappled pattern
Flowing hyperostosis resembling dripping candle wax on radiographs

redFlags: Progressive bone deformities causing functional impairment
Signs of systemic involvement such as anemia or neurological symptoms
references: Schinzel A. et al. (1995). Dappled diaphyseal dysplasia: clinical and radiological features. Am J Med Genet.
Rosenberg A.E. (2014). Bone Dysplasias: Radiologic-Pathologic Correlations. Elsevier
